region.text: Donji Kraji (Kljuc, Soko Grad) and Usora (Srebrenik), the zones of Louis I's 1363 campaign

ledger.note: 1363: Louis I of Hungary invades Bosnia. 'In 1363, a conflict broke out between the two men'; 'An army led by Louis himself attacked Donji Kraji, where the nobility was divided in its loyalties between Tvrtko and Louis'; 'A month later an army led by the Palatine of Hungary Nicholas Kont ... struck Usora'. Vlatko Vukoslavic 'deserted to Louis and surrendered to him the important fortress of Kljuc', but Vukac Hrvatinic held Soko Grad in Pliva and the Hungarians retreated; Srebrenik in Usora 'held out against a massive attack' ('Tvrtko's first victory against the Hungarian king', Tvrtko I page, which has the same account and gives Louis's stated aim, to eradicate the Bosnian heretics). Donji Kraji had been given to Louis as the 1357 dowry, but its nobles' loyalty was split, so it is drawn as contested ground, not as Hungarian land; kingdom-of-hungary /ledger/54 has the matching contest_start.

ledger.note: March 1366: the contest over Donji Kraji and Usora ends when Tvrtko, who had fled to Louis's court after the magnates' revolt of February 1366, returns 'in March' with Louis's likely military aid ('provided Tvrtko with aid (likely military)') and 'reestablished control over a part of the country ... including Donji Kraji, Rama, Hum, and Usora'. The fighting itself ended in 1363 (the Hungarian retreat, Srebrenik held); the later end date follows the land, which the pages show unsettled until 1366. kingdom-of-hungary ends its contest in March 1367 (/ledger/57): one year apart, because the Banate and Tvrtko pages give no year for the return (both have 'Vuk 1366-1367' and Tvrtko as last ban from 1367).

ledger.note: March 1366: Tvrtko returns from exile and regains Donji Kraji, Rama and Hum. 'Tvrtko returned to Bosnia in March and reestablished control over a part of the country by the end of the month, including the areas of Donji Kraji, Rama (where he then resided), Hum, and Usora.' Corrected after review: (1) the counterpart is the rebel magnates who had 'dethroned him' in February 1366 and replaced him with his brother Vuk, not Hungary; the page does not say whom he took the lands from (context implies the magnates and Vuk's supporters), and Louis, who had welcomed him, 'provided Tvrtko with aid (likely military)'; the pages do not say Louis gave the 1357 dowry lands back (kingdom-of-hungary records a loss to Bosnia in March 1367). (2) Usora and Soli are dropped from the region: the ledger never loses them after 1324 (Srebrenik held in 1363), although the page lists Usora among the areas he reestablished control over. (3) The year is the dossier's reading of an undated 'March': the Tvrtko page's infobox says 'interrupted by Vuk, 1366-1367', Sanko defected to Vuk in late 1366 and Vuk fled to Ragusa in 1367, so Tvrtko held only part of the country from March 1366 and all of it in 1367.

wars.name: Hungarian crusade against Bosnia
wars.outcome: Coloman of Hungary, ban from 1235, holds most of Bosnia until his death at Mohi in 1241; Ninoslav retreats to Dubrovnik in 1240 and restores control over most of Bosnia in 1241.

wars.name: Hungarian invasion of Bosnia (Louis I)
wars.outcome: Louis I attacks Donji Kraji in spring 1363 and a month later the Palatine Nicholas Kont strikes Usora; Vlatko Vukoslavic surrenders Kljuc, but Soko Grad and Srebrenik hold and the Hungarians withdraw ('Tvrtko's first victory against the Hungarian king'); the magnates' unity then wanes and they dethrone Tvrtko in February 1366.
wars.note: Tvrtko I page: 'By April, the King had begun amassing an army'; Ragusa ordered its merchants out of Bosnia in May. The Banate page's 'in February the following year' would give 1364 for the revolt but its own Stanak paragraph and ruler list (Tvrtko 1353-1366, Vuk 1366-1367) give 1366.

notes: Page budget (5) spent on the Banate article, Stephen II, Tvrtko I, Matej Ninoslav and Ban Kulin. The Banate and the Kingdom of Bosnia are one continuous state ('elevated to a kingdom' in 1377); Cliopatria keeps two rows and carries the banate row to 1384, so the 1375 shape (1377-1384) belongs to the kingdom-of-bosnia dossier: the colour agent should give both one colour (family balkans). Hungarian overlordship of Kulin ('nominal vassal to Hungarian king', 1180s), Byzantine overlordship 1167-1180 and Stjepan I's vassal-banship to the Subic (1290-1314) are not written as vassal events: the vassal_start/_end events belong to the suzerain's dossier (kingdom-of-hungary, byzantine-empire); a gap-filler should add them there. The pages give no dates for the capitals (Visoko, Bobovac, Sutjeska), no infobox area, and no extent for Kulin's Bosnia; the Cliopatria shape at 1188-1240 is accepted as drawn. The 1241 loss event is confidence 1. Counterparts without dossiers: Subic of Bribir, Nicholas Altomanovic (a Serbian magnate; the serbian-empire dossier may carry his lands). Usora and Soli: the Stephen II page puts them in Serbian hands until Milutin's death (1321) and the Banate page has the Hungarian crown annex them; the 1324 counterpart is kingdom-of-serbia on the Stephen II page alone. Gazetteer names needed: Zahumlje, Donji Kraji, Usora, Soli, Polimlje, Zagorje (Herzegovina), Konavli, Visoko, Jajce. REVIEW FIXES: (1) The 1363 Hungarian invasion is now a war and a contest (1363 to March 1366) with kingdom-of-hungary over Donji Kraji and Usora; the keyframe 1357-1365 is split into 1357-1362 (without Donji Kraji and western Hum) and 1363-1365 (Donji Kraji and Usora kept as contested ground, western Hum out). (2) The March 1366 gain no longer re-adds Usora and Soli and is from the rebel magnates and Vuk; the Hungarian dossier ends its contest in March 1367. (3) The 1377 Trebinje, Konavli and Dracevica gain is from Djuradj I Balsic (Zeta), a counterpart without a dossier (suggested slug balsici). (4) The start in 1180 is a choice: the Banate page's infobox has 'First known Ban (Ban Boric): 1154', and the Ban Boric page has Boric appointed ban in 1154 'during Byzantine-Hungarian conflicts', an ally (not a vassal) of Hungary, last mentioned in 1163, and Bosnia a Byzantine province from ca. 1166; Cliopatria starts in 1188 and the first sovereign act is Kulin's independence in 1180, so the dossier starts there. (5) The 1241 loss stays a confidence-1 Cliopatria event: the Prijezda I page dates Bela IV's division of Bosnia (Usora and Soli to Rastislav) to 1253. (6) The c. 1326 Zavrsje gain stays 'nobody': the Zavrsje page is a disambiguation page and no page opened names the holder.
